#1880. Why Arsenal failed with Max Dowman red card appeal as FA release statement

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal youngster Max Dowman "gave the referee a decision to make" after being sent off against Fleetwood Town last month, a Football Association (FA) commission has found.

The 16-year-old was shown a straight red card late on at Highbury Stadium, compounding a miserable night for the Gunners as they were sent tumbling out of the Carabao Cup at the fourth round by the League Two side on penalties.

Dowman was given his marching orders for kicking out after a heavy challenge from Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal.

As reported by Standard Sport, Arsenal decided to appeal the red card and, as per the BBC, submitted two videos as evidence to the FA's regulatory commission, along with a letter from secretary Zayna Perkins.

However, the appeal was rejected - meaning Dowman must serve a three-match domestic suspension.

Dowman’s sanction was determined by a three-person Independent Regulatory Commission, who have released the written reasons for their decisions.

The majority view accepted that Dowman had received a forceful challenge that he did not see coming, but the two commission members felt he had the option to "step out of this challenge without any reaction but he turned back towards Neal and his forceful attempt at a retaliatory kick gave the referee a decision to make".

The minority view was that Dowman's actions were petulant rather than an act of violent conduct, and "did not constitute a challenge made with excessive force or brutality.”

The forward's age was rejected as a relevant factor in deliberations and the commission could find no "truly exceptional" reason to alter the suspension.

While Arsenal felt a three-game ban was "clearly excessive", the appeal was unanimously rejected by the commission members, who also noted that the threshold for a "clearly excessive" appeal is a high bar to reach.

Dowman served the first of his three-match ban in the win over Liverpool last weekend and will sit out Premier League matches against Hull and Newcastle either side of the November international break.

#1879. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”

Gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”

Here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY

He says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu

Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car company, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton said yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

#1878. Romano: Another renewal and two targets – the moves for Milan after Pulisic’s extension

AC Milan are looking to build on their derby win and surge up the table, while the management continue to plan for the future.

Important developments came in the past few days, starting with the renewal of Christian Pulisic’s contract until 2031 which was made official on Friday, the day before he opened the scoring against Inter with a header.

On the night of the game, Fabrizio Romano confirmed that an agreement in principle had been reached with Markus Krösche to become the new Head of Football. It also seems that the extension of Adrien Rabiot – another derby hero – isn’t far away either.

Romano gave an update last night in a video on his YouTube channel, explaining what the planned moves are for Milan during what is a potentially decisive stage in their project.

“There’s work to be done and construction to be done, even in terms of contracts. The next player to be renewed will be Rabiot. AC Milan is working hard on this signing. Rabiot is the symbol of AC Milan’s intelligent operations. The club wants to secure him,” he said (via MilanNews).

“Then there’s the transfer market. Milan wants to present themselves with confidence. The defender they didn’t sign in the summer could arrive in January. I mentioned Gonçalo Inacio’s name last week and I’ll continue to mention it.

“He remains a highly sought-after player. There are other options, but the defender is a key issue for Milan. It won’t end here. I expect a move in attack, and Milan will certainly do something other than the defender.”

#1877. Tottenham: Vinai Venkatesham reveals bold Spurs target and confirms 'plan' for relegation

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Vinai Venkatesham has insisted that Tottenham are targeting winning the Champions League under Roberto De Zerbi.

Spurs have finished 17th in the Premier League in each of the past two seasons, narrowly avoiding relegation to the Championship on the final day of last term.

De Zerbi arrived in March to help steer the club to safety after Thomas Frank’s stumbling reign and a disastrous interim period under Igor Tudor.

Tottenham sat winless and bottom of the table at the first international break this season but results have picked up since then. Three successive wins have left them in ninth place ahead of Saturday’s lunchtime trip to Leeds.

Venkatesham is confident that Spurs are now “on the right track” under De Zerbi and the club’s chief executive was ambitious when talking about long-term targets.

Speaking on The Sports Agents podcast, Venkatesham revealed the extremely lofty goals he believes are possible after a period of upheaval to bring in De Zerbi and overhaul the squad.

He said: “Ultimately, I guess the best way to answer your question is what are we here for? We’re here to win, right? The people that we’ve attracted to the football club, the long list of people, everyone is here to win.

“If you work for Tottenham, when we talk about being here to win, that means we’re here to win the Premier League. That’s what this football club wants to do.

“It wants to win the Premier League and it wants to be consistent in the Champions League and it wants to ultimately win the Champions League.

“Can I tell you what year that’s going to happen in? Obviously I can’t but that’s what we’re aiming for and that’s what I want every single person that works for this club to think about every single day.

#1876. Raphinha responds to Flick fears after Ancelotti talks

By Naim Beneddra | 05 Nov 2026 22:12

Barcelona captain Raphinha has moved to ease Hansi Flick's concerns over his upcoming international commitments, revealing that he has already discussed his fitness and playing time with Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti.

The 29-year-old, who signed a contract extension until June 2030 on Thursday, admitted that he is still not fully fit after suffering another muscular problem while representing his country earlier this season.

His comments come just days after Flick publicly questioned the demands of another lengthy international trip, particularly given that Raphinha returned injured from Brazil's previous training camp.

However, the former Leeds United attacker insists that Ancelotti understands his situation and will take his recovery into account during November's friendlies against Japan and Singapore.

The reassurance comes at an important time for Barcelona, with Raphinha enjoying the most prolific start to a season of his career and several demanding fixtures approaching.

Speaking to reporters following the announcement of his new Barcelona contract, Raphinha addressed the concerns surrounding his participation in Brazil's upcoming matches.

The forward confirmed that he had already spoken with Ancelotti about his physical condition and the importance of managing his workload.

"Ancelotti, as a coach, knows he has to distribute playing time," Raphinha explained, as quoted by Barca Blaugranes.

"He knows that an injury would be complicated for Brazil too, and he knows how to manage minutes.

"We've spoken; he knows I'm recovering from an injury. I'm fine, but not 100%. Barça fans shouldn't worry because I'm taking good care of myself."

The admission that he has yet to regain full fitness is particularly significant given his recent injury history.

Raphinha suffered a hamstring problem during Brazil's international commitments in October, forcing him to return to Barcelona for treatment.

The setback ruled him out of two club matches, adding to concerns surrounding a player who has experienced several muscular injuries over the past year.

He also suffered an injury while representing Brazil against France in March, subsequently missing Barcelona's Champions League quarter-final against Atletico Madrid.

Another physical problem during the 2026 World Cup prevented him from featuring in the latter stages of Brazil's campaign.

Those setbacks explain why Flick was uneasy about the forward undertaking another long-distance journey so soon after his latest recovery.

Speaking on October 30, the Barcelona manager acknowledged that he had discussed Raphinha's situation with sporting director Deco.

"After the last international break, he came back injured, which wasn't ideal," Flick explained.

The German coach also made it clear that he would welcome a cautious approach from Brazil's coaching staff.

"If he can manage his playing time well, I'll be happy. Travelling to Singapore isn't ideal, but it's beyond my control."

The comments reflected Barcelona's concern over the demands of international football rather than any suggestion that Raphinha should abandon his commitments to Brazil.

Ancelotti's side are scheduled to face Japan on November 14 before meeting Singapore three days later, with both fixtures taking place in Singapore.

Raphinha's latest remarks offer some reassurance that his condition has been discussed with the Brazil manager, although he did not disclose any specific agreement regarding the number of minutes he will play.

The timing of the international break is especially sensitive for Barcelona because of Raphinha's extraordinary influence this season.

The Brazilian has scored 19 goals in just 13 appearances across all competitions, including 15 in La Liga and four in the Champions League.

His performances have helped Flick's side establish themselves at the top of the Spanish league, while his adaptation to a more central attacking role has made him an even greater threat in front of goal.

Previously deployed primarily on the wing, Raphinha has increasingly operated as a centre-forward, taking advantage of his movement and finishing ability inside the penalty area.

His form was rewarded on Thursday when Barcelona officially confirmed a contract extension keeping him at Camp Nou until June 2030.

The agreement provides further evidence of his importance to the club, particularly after a period in which his future had previously been the subject of transfer speculation.

However, Barcelona's immediate priority will be ensuring that their captain remains available during a demanding period of the campaign.

Flick's side travel to Atletico Madrid on Sunday for a crucial La Liga encounter, with only two points separating the clubs at the top of the standings.

They also have a Champions League meeting with Manchester City to negotiate after the international break, increasing the importance of Raphinha returning from Brazil without another setback.

The forward's situation presents a delicate balancing act for both managers.

Ancelotti will want to make use of one of Brazil's most productive attacking players, while Flick is understandably reluctant to risk losing a footballer who has become central to Barcelona's ambitions.

For now, Raphinha's discussion with the Brazil manager suggests that his recent fitness problems have been taken into consideration.

Nevertheless, his acknowledgement that he is still below full fitness means Barcelona will be watching his involvement in the November friendlies particularly closely.

AC Milan’s defensive performance was largely solid against a prolific Inter attack, and Sankhoun Diawara played his part.

As MilanNews write, Diawara has gone from a semi-unknown prospect to a potentially key asset in the space of a few weeks. After his strong performance against Udinese and his more difficult performance against Bologna, there was some surprise when he was named as a starter vs. Inter.

#1873. SC Paderborn vs Eintracht Frankfurt - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 05 Nov 2026 22:17

Hoping to distance themselves from the Bundesliga's relegation zone, SC Paderborn will welcome European hopefuls Eintracht Frankfurt to Home Deluxe Arena on Saturday.

The hosts are searching for their second win in six games, while Die Adler could earn a third on the bounce.

Ralf Kettemann's Paderborn have performed admirably since making the step up from the second division, but they will be looking over their shoulder ahead of a tough challenge this weekend.

Saturday's hosts are currently 14th in the Bundesliga with nine points, sitting just two above 16th-placed Union Berlin in the relegation playoff spot.

Last time out, Kettemann's side were held to a 0-0 draw by Borussia Monchengladbach, failing to score for the second successive match.

In fact, only Schalke 04 have netted fewer than Paderborn's six goals in the German top flight this season, a concerning trait that the manager will be need to address in order to stave off the threat of demotion.

That being said, the promoted club have maintained an impressive defensive record so far, with Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich the only teams to have conceded less than their nine in eight matches.

Another positive for the hosts is the fact a win could lift them into the top half, considering they are level on points with every club up to 10th-placed Augsburg, and are just one behind ninth-placed Mainz 05.

Meanwhile, Adi Hutter's Frankfurt have been inconsistent for the majority of the 2026-27 campaign so far, though the club will be keen to prove they have turned a corner.

Die Adler beat Hamburger SV 3-1 at home last time out, and by the same score away in the DFB-Pokal just days earlier, marking the first time they have recorded back-to-back wins this season.

That latest success has Hutter's men eighth with 11 points, just two shy of sixth-placed Bayer Leverkusen in the race for Europe.

Heading into Saturday's showdown, Frankfurt have now won three of their last four outings across all competitions, only succumbing to a 1-0 defeat at Dortmund on October 24.

However, the visitors have come out on top in just one of their four Bundesliga away games this term - downing Mainz 3-1 in mid-September - while conceding 11 goals in the process.

Eintracht Frankfurt form (all competitions):

Paderborn will be without Marcel Hoffmeier due to a thigh injury, as well as fellow centre-back Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant, who returned to training late last month but is still building fitness after a lengthy layoff.

In their absence, Tjark Scheller, Mattes Hansen and Jano ter Horst look set to start in Kettemann's three-man defence, flanked by wing-backs Laurin Curda and Raphael Obermair.

Elsewhere, midfielder Timur Gayret remains sidelined with a knee injury, though Santiago Castaneda, Tom Baack and Gabriel Vidovic should be on hand to operate in the centre of the park.

As for Frankfurt, they are missing long-term absentee Jessic Ngankam, who is continuing his recovery from a thigh injury, while attacking midfielder Mario Gotze is a doubt due to an ear infection that caused him to miss training on Wednesday and Thursday.

With that in mind, striker Jonathan Burkardt will be supported by a trio of Ritsu Doan, Can Uzun and Fares Chaibi on Saturday.

There are also question marks bout the fitness of centre-half Robin Koch, who only trained partially this week after picking up a knock to his knee, but Lilian Brassier and Jeremiaha Maluze will be ready to line up at the heart of Hutter's defence if he is unavailable.

Noll; Scheller, Hansen, Ter Horst; Curda, Vidovic, Baack, Castaneda, Obermair; Tigges, Marino

Eintracht Frankfurt possible starting lineup:

Atubolu; Knauff, Brassier, Maluze, Baum; Onyedika, Aseko-Nkili; Doan, Uzun, Chaibi; Burkardt

Paderborn have struggled to score this season, but given their commendable record at the back, they are unlikely to suffer a thrashing this weekend.

Frankfurt will be buoyed by their improved results in recent weeks, though they will need to defy their form on the road to secure all three points, so expect to see a close-fought game.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Under-21 regular Byfield was handed his maiden senior Tottenham debut back in January, when former boss Thomas Frank introduced him in place of Lucas Bergvall for the final 28 minutes of a 2-0 home Champions League win over Borussia Dortmund.

Byfield has been building his fitness since then and was seen in a club video posted to social media returning to first-team training at Tottenham on Thursday, alongside fellow youngster Luca Williams-Barnett, who was handed his own Premier League debut by head coach Roberto De Zerbi during last weekend’s win over Crystal Palace.

It remains to be seen if De Zerbi will consider Byfield for a potential first-team role in the months ahead, with the likes of Tyrese Hall having also impressed the Spurs boss during a recent warm-weather training camp in Marbella, alongside Tye Hall and Callum Olusesi.

#1870. Barnsley vs Aldershot Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 05 Nov 2026 22:18, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:00

Aldershot Town will set out to pull off an FA Cup first-round upset in South Yorkshire on Saturday, when they visit Oakwell to take on third-tier Barnsley.

The hosts enter at this stage while their visitors took part in the final qualifying round and needed a replay to progress.

Barnsley head into FA Cup action for the first time this season on Saturday in need of a victory to arrest a slump in the early stages of 2026-27.

The Reds reached the third round of this competition last year, falling in a trip to Liverpool, but begin their new campaign with just four wins from 17 competitive matches so far this term with all of those coming in the first six outings.

They did enjoy a positive start to life back under returning boss Daniel Stendel but are now winless in 11 games since early September, losing nine of those including four straight league defeats heading into the weekend.

Stendel's men were, at least, able to end that rut at home to Oxford United on Saturday, drawing 1-1 thanks to Vimal Yoganathan's opener having been down to 10 men inside 10 minutes, but the South Yorkshire side still sit 23rd in League One with just nine points on the board from 12 games having conceded 22 goals.

With positives to take from the weekend's display but real cause for concern around their recent months, Barnsley will be desperate to avoid an upset at the weekend and taste victory at Oakwell.

Their opponents, meanwhile, make the trip north having scraped through the final qualifying round in the FA Cup.

Aldershot Town entered this year's competition in the fourth and final round of qualifying, taking on ninth-tier Tadley Calleva, but they were only able to draw 2-2 at home before prevailing in a 2-0 triumph on the road in the replay.

That eventual cup win broke up a five-game losing run in the National League for the Shots, who also headed into the weekend in the midst of a rut, but they bounced back to winning ways at home to Gateshead, as Brody Peart scored the only goal inside five minutes.

Scott Davies's side climbed back up to 14th spot in the fifth tier with that result, and now on the back of a midweek National League Cup loss to Ipswich Town Under-21s, they will hope to defy the odds at Oakwell on Saturday to reach the FA Cup second round for just the second time since 2015.

Barnsley are set to remain without attackers Ben Hamed Toure and Fabio Jalo on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Stendel should field a near full-strength XI with the Reds desperate for a win to turn their fortunes round, meaning star man Reyes Cleary should continue on the wing, while Tobi Adeyemo was injured early on Saturday and may be replaced up front by Rylan Brownlie.

Veteran and recent signing Daniel Johnson may be afforded a start in midfield alongside either Luca Connell or Patrick Kelly, while Jack Shepherd is available at the back despite being sent off last time out in the league.

Aldershot Town will field a similar starting XI from last week's league win over Gateshead.

Marcus Dinanga and Marcus Wyllie will both hope to start in attack, but if they continue with a 4-2-3-1 shape the line should again be led by Tristan Abrahams, who has scored six goals so far this season.

A summer of plenty of change added several key men to their ranks, with Michael Stickland and Kiki Oshilaja now mainstays in defence and Dominic Odusanya and Conor Lawless likely to continue a midfield partnership if the latter is fit having been forced off last weekend.

Slicker; Kay, Gale, Shepherd, Larkeche; Connell, Johnson; Yoganathan, McGeegan, Cleary; Brownlie

Hayes; Stickland, Oshilaja, Dyce, Harfield; Lawless, Odusanya; Peart, Tuma, Sandah; Abrahams

Barnsley could certainly be vulnerable to a cup upset at home, given their poor league record and struggles at both ends of the pitch and growing concern around the club, but needing a win to start turning their form around, we do expect Stendel's men to outclass their non-league visitors.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Thomas Tuchel has explained his “difficult decision” to leave Arsenal winger Noni Madueke out of the latest England squad.

Despite having been one of Tuchel’s trusted men at the World Cup in the summer, Madueke was on Friday omitted for Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

The snub comes after England team-mate Bukayo Saka’s quad injury had given Madueke a greater opportunity to impress for Arsenal on the right flank of late.

He has played more in recent weeks and scored important goals against Nottingham Forest in the Premier League and Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

But despite call-ups for Arsenal team-mates Ezri Konsa, Declan Rice, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ben White and Eberechi Eze, Madueke was left out by England this time.

“It was a close call and a difficult decision not to bring Noni, because he got his minutes after Bukayo’s injury at Arsenal,” Tuchel said at a post-squad selection press conference at Wembley.

“He got some goals. It was very close. But also [in that position], we stuck with the group that we had [during the last international break] and give them our trust.”

White was injured during the last international window so not available for selection.

He was England’s only goalscorer in March, when he made his first appearances for the national team since leaving the 2022 World Cup squad in Qatar during Gareth Southgate’s tenure for personal reasons.

White was booed by some sections of the England fanbase during friendlies against Uruguay and Japan at Wembley, but Tuchel saw that as no reason to omit him from this month’s squad now the player is back fit.

“We were not happy about this,” Tuchel said on the boos for White, who also missed out on a World Cup place due to injury. “We could understand the disappointment of the fans, of course, with what had happened before. But I think this is expressed [by] now and should be a closed book.

Former Salford City manager Karl Robinson is in the running for the Bromley job and could be joined in the dugout by a Premier League icon.

#1867. Thomas Tuchel doubles down on Cole Palmer warning as England snub explained

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Thomas Tuchel has explained why Cole Palmer was left out of the latest England squad, repeating his belief that the Chelsea star “misses too many opportunities to impress” for his country.

Palmer was on Friday the headline omission from Tuchel’s 25-man squad to contest this month’s Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

That was despite England staff checking with Chelsea on his fitness this week in the lead-up to the squad being finalised. It is understood that Palmer is fit and was available for selection.

Having missed the World Cup in the summer, Palmer was initially picked for the last England squad in September, but withdrew due to an injury which Chelsea said they needed to manage.

While Tuchel acknowledged at the time that the issue was genuine, he did not hide his disappointment and remarked that Palmer “misses too many opportunities” to play for England.

Of Tuchel’s 26 matches in charge so far, Palmer has featured in only three. The England head coach was asked at a press conference at Wembley on Friday why Palmer had been overlooked.

“It’s enough No10s and we stick to the guys who were in camp [last time],” Tuchel explained. “The impact of all the players was immense.

“We have Josh King as a new player. He can play all four [attacking] positions. That’s basically the reason. He gives us a bit of flexibility.

“In the pre-season, he [King] helped us in training as a full-back. We will not try that again.”

Tuchel provided further detail about Palmer’s situation, insisting: “Everyone is desperate to play for England, and Cole is no exception.

“But, again, what I said last time: he misses too many opportunities to impress. Two-and-a-half weeks was a long time [to miss]. The door is always open, but nothing has changed, and we decided [to go] without him.”

There was a first senior England call-up for Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham, the younger brother of Real Madrid star Jude.

Tuchel hinted that Jobe Bellingham could come into his thinking as he plots out his midfield selection for the clash with Croatia next week.

“Myles [Lewis-Skelly] is suspended for the first game against Croatia, so there is an opportunity [for Jobe] - coming on his own pathway,” he said.

Tuchel then explained why Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, much-tipped for a maiden England call by team-mates at Everton and manager David Moyes, had not been selected.

“[He was ] close, a very good player,” Tuchel said. “I see him as an offensive No8 or more as a No10.

“As you know, he is in our squad of 55. He is a standout player for Everton; you see his quality. He was very close.”

#1866. Charlton Athletic vs Sheffield United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 05 Nov 2026 22:29

Aiming to continue their climb up the Championship table and break into the playoff places, Sheffield United will head to The Valley to take on Charlton Athletic on Saturday.

Back-to-back victories have seen the visitors move within a point of the top eight, while their visitors sit four points above the drop zone after four straight losses.

Charlton Athletic return to action at the weekend aiming to end a dismal run of Championship form and arrest a drop towards the relegation zone.

Following a 19th-placed finish in their first season back in the second tier last time around, the Addicks won their first three league matches of the new term but have since drawn five and lost six of 11 matches.

In those games, Nathan Jones's side have scored just six goals and conceded 20, dropping to 21st spot in the process, just one place and four points above Burnley in the drop zone.

They have now suffered four straight defeats heading into their final match before the international break, falling to Watford, Norwich City and Middlesbrough before they hosted newly-promoted Bolton Wanderers on Tuesday and again came away empty-handed as Sam Dalby scored the only goal inside 20 minutes at the Valley.

With pressure surely growing on Jones, and the international break arguably coming at a decent time to arrest Charlton's slump, they will be desperate to put a win on the board to increase their lead over the drop zone ahead of the return to action.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to London aiming to carry an upturn in form into the break.

Unlike the hosts, Sheffield United are now bouncing back from a slow start to the Championship season, having set out to challenge for promotion this term only to pick up just nine points from their first eight matches before the opening break of the season.

Chris Wilder's men have reversed their fortunes since, though, putting 13 more points on the board in six outings courtesy of four wins and a draw alongside a solitary away defeat to Portsmouth.

Following a 1-0 home victory over Wrexham on Friday, the Blades headed to strugglers Preston North End on Tuesday and came from 1-0 down to win 3-2 thanks to Sydie Peck's first-half hat-trick, leaving them on 22 points from 14 matches with just five teams conceding fewer than the 17 goals they have allowed.

Now in a much better position in ninth spot, and just one point behind eighth-placed West Ham United, Sheffield United will look to make it three straight wins with the chance to head into the second break of the campaign in the playoff places.

Charlton Athletic remain unable to call on winger Rob Apter, who has been sidelined since early September.

In their midweek defeat, Jones replaced midfielder Nathaniel Chalobah with attacker Miles Leaburn at half time and could go with a more attacking shape from the outset at the weekend with Leaburn, Matt Godden, Sonny Carey and Millenic Alli all competing for attacking spots.

That is after Charlie Kelman led the line against Bolton with support from Harvey Knibbs, Karlan Grant and top scorer Tyreece Campbell, while Conor Coventry is a mainstay in the engine room and Will Mannion was preferred in net over Arthur Okonkwo last time out.

Sheffield United are without forwards Patrick Bamford and Ryan One and midfielder Joe Rothwell, while Kalvin Phillips was also absent in midweek but may be fit to feature.

He is unlikely to be rushed back, though, and Wilder should field a similar starting XI from their midweek away win, meaning Jairo Riedewald may again partner Peck, who decided that game with his hat-trick, while Liam Kitching should come straight back into the defence after serving a one-match suspension on Tuesday.

In a 4-4-2 shape, they may again be flanked by Romelle Donovan and Tahith Chong with Ben Brereton Diaz, Tom Cannon, Tyrese Campbell and Oliver Arblaster competing for attacking spots in Bamford's absence.

Sheffield United appear to be hitting their stride since the season's first international break and have ground out several hard-fought wins in recent weeks, while the hosts seem unable to arrest a slump and we fancy Wilder's men to take all three points again with their sights set on the top eight.

#1865. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV

"Since the new manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9

Dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

Smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

The noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

Bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

Murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

The current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

Safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

Newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

The pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

Jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls new signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

It looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

Newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

Wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

Just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

Newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

We are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

Three @premierleague games ✅Two @premierleague goals ✅ pic.twitter.com/B46guzqUjm

A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Two goals in two minutes leaves it intriguingly poisedIt's Newcastle 1-2 Bournemouth at half-time pic.twitter.com/iqTsAKRuVF

There will be three minutes of added time to finish off this breathless first half. Can Newcastle find a late leveller before the break or will Bournemouth restore their two-goal advantage?

It’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

What a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0

St James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

Newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Bournemouth’s high press works again and the ball breaks loose to Kluivert. He shoots from range and his deflected strike flies narrowly wide of the post.

Elanga’s frustrating afternoon continues as he collides with Silva as both players compete for the ball. The Newcastle winger picks up the game’s first yellow card because of the challenge.

You would expect a lot more from Tavernier there, but Bournemouth look so dangerous going forward.

Bournemouth defend a couple of Newcastle corners in quick succession. The hosts are yet to create a notable chance.

There’s a real intensity to this game. Bournemouth are attempting to match Newcastle’s pace and physicality in every department. Just now, there was a really interesting battle between Willock and Adams, with the Newcastle man eventually winning a free-kick after a strong dribble.

Bournemouth should be two in front. A terrible pass from Sven Botman gifted the Brazilian the ball on the edge of the Newcastle box but he failed to hit the target.

Newcastle are rattled. They have not got to grips with Bournemouth in midfield and they are crowding out Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock whenever Matthias Jaissle’s side look to go direct.

We wondered how Newcastle would match up against Bournemouth and they have looked second best so far.

What a chance for Bournemouth to double their lead! What is Botman doing? The centre-back misplaces a pass and Evanilson latches onto the mistake. The striker runs in on goal, but blazes the glaring opportunity over the bar. That’s a huge let-off for Newcastle. Evanilson must do better from that range.

Scott’s deflected strike richochets into Tavernier’s path, with the Bournemouth attacker sneaking in behind Dedic, who switches off. Tavernier then directs a half-volley into the roof of the net. Newcastle are furious. They feel they should of been awarded a free-kick after a earlier tussle between Truffert and Elanga. Both players are pulling each other’s shirts. After a quick VAR check, the goal stands and the away fans are delighted.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Dedic shows his quality by intercepting a pass from deep, skipping away from Scott’s sliding challenge and then dribbling all the way to the byline. He can’t quite win a corner, but his efforts are appreciated by the Newcastle faithful.

Newcastle attempt to counter through Wissa and Willock, with the latter passing to Barnes. However, the former Leicester man cuts inside and runs into trouble, causing the opening to disappear.

Tavernier takes it and fires a low effort around the wall, but Hornicek is there to get down low and make a relatively routine save.

Elanga has made a busy start to this game. The winger’s pace is so explosive. Bournemouth then win a free-kick on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area as Miley catches Kluivert. Mulitple Bournemouth players are standing over this.

The visitors get us under way at St James’ Park. Which German manager will prevail?

Newcastle are in their iconic black and white strip, while Bournemouth are sporting an eye-catching purple away kit. We are just minutes away from kick-off. St James’ Park is in full voice.

An unchanged line up for Newcastle United in Matthias Jaissle’s third Premier League game as manager but this is a very different sort of challenge.

Despite having a miserable record against Bournemouth in recent years, Newcastle will be expected to win this afternoon. The atmosphere, electric for the opener against Liverpool and the return of villain Alexander Isak, will be more expectant today.

These are the fixtures Eddie Howe’s team repeatedly slipped up in at home last season, where the likes of Everton, Brentford, Bournemouth and Sunderland all won.

Can Jaissle improve that record? Can his team thrive when they are likely to have more of the ball, play against a low block defence and an opponent adept at lightning-fast counterattacks?

Does the German’s “vertical” football have as much success against a team that does not play a high defensive line as Liverpool and Tottenham did?

We are likely to know a lot more about Newcastle after this game. There has been a lot of hype and excitement after an impressive start to the new season but have people got a little carried away?

Let’s see how they get on against a Bournemouth side that probably should have got at least a point away to Manchester City in their opening away game.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets in the spring, Matías Fernandez-Pardo featured prominently.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1864. GdS: How Amorim’s fluidity helped Rabiot record career-best start to a season

Adrien Rabiot continues to deliver in the biggest games for AC Milan, and Ruben Amorim is arguably getting the best ever form out of him.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by recalling how different things were in the summer. With Milan falling to fifth and Massmiliano Allegri being sacked, many presumed that Rabiot could follow him to Napoli, to play Champions League football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Rabiot not only remained at Milanello, but is also the Atlas of the team this year. He carries it on his shoulders and takes its weight with disarming ease and personality. While Allegri observes Milan from below, Adrien has found a new coach who is giving him a new lease of life.

The derby goal is an excellent indicator of Rabiot’s confidence, attempting that billiard-like shot (even though some, like Yunus Musah, maintain it was a cross) in a match like this, with the game still wide open, signifies complete self-confidence.

The Frenchman knows perfectly well he has a powerful shot, but he opted for finesse, guiding the ball to kiss the post and land in the back of the net as eleven Nerazzurri players watched it slowly and mockingly cross their penalty area.

Rabiot was one of the derby’s heroes but has been performing at a high level for several matches now. He currently has the best average rating in the squad, and it’s a stratospheric 6.81 (out of 10, across all games).

The other key number is nine: five goals and four assists this season makes nine contributions, the most in the squad. In the league, he’s been involved in a goal in each of his last five games: assists against Lazio, goals against Lecce and Sassuolo, a goal and assist against Atalanta, and a goal in the derby.

To better understand his further improvement from an already very high level, we must consider that in the entire last season, Adrien had six goals and four assists. He’s one goal away from matching that tally.

Some tactical considerations help contextualise things. Compared to Allegri, Amorim’s style of football is on another level, being much more attacking. It’s not based solely on counter-attacks, but on a flow of play that starts from midfield and allows for the runs of those who move in between the lines.

Rabiot has always been a player who can get forward: he has the physique, technique, and footballing intelligence. Amorim has given him a further step because he’s made him more difficult to read for opponents.

If before, the Frenchman was a classic pivot midfielder, now you find him practically everywhere. At the start of the season, Amorim’s style of football was positional, locked into a 3-4-2-1 that seemed set in stone with Rabiot behind the striker.

Then the Portuguese coach realised he was doing himself harm and began a tactical overhaul. The fundamentalist has become fluid, and the playing system is now an abstract concept that must be filled with individual interpretations.

This is a set of circumstances where Rabiot shines. The derby is a perfect example: the former PSG man was everywhere, depending on his own tendencies and the team’s need for certain characteristics in certain parts if the pitch.

This is the best start to a season of his career. Now, in addition to the pitch, he’ll also have to keep an eye on his desk. After Strahinja Pavlovic and Christian Pulisic, he’s the next one destined to ascend to the fourth floor of Casa Milan to sign a renewal waiting for him.

#1862. Minnesota United vs San Jose Earthquakes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 05 Nov 2026 22:31, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:18

Minnesota United and San Jose Earthquakes draw the curtain on their 2026 Major League Soccer regular season campaign when they lock horns at Allianz Field on Sunday morning.

While the home side head into the league finale needing maximum points to stand a chance of securing back-to-back playoff appearances, San Jose will aim to finish the campaign strong and gather momentum ahead of the post-season quest.

A strong showing at the business end of the season has put Minnesota United in contention for playoff qualification ahead of a crunch final-day showdown, with the Loons securing a 3-1 win over Los Angeles FC on Monday to maintain their newfound form.

Joaquin Pereyra turned in an eye-catching display at the BMO Stadium, netting on either side of Cherrion Valerius’s 34th-minute strike to put the visitors three goals up, before Sergio Vasquez pulled one back for Los Angeles FC in the 89th minute.

Coming off a 3-1 victory over Sporting Kansas City on October 29, Minnesota United have now picked up three wins in their most recent four outings and are unbeaten in six straight matches (3W 3D), having lost each of the five games preceding this run.

This late-season resurgence has seen Cameron Knowles’s men surge into 12th place in the Western Conference standings with 41 points from 33 matches, just two points behind ninth-placed Colorado Rapids in the final playoff qualifying spot.

Attacking improvements have been integral in Minnesota’s upturn in form, with 2+ goals scored in five of their last six games, and they will also hope to make home advantage count against an opposing side who have failed to win their last six league visits to Allianz Field, losing four and claiming two draws since a 3-1 victory in May 2018.

Having seen their form take a dip in recent weeks, San Jose Earthquakes finally rediscovered their winning touch last Saturday when they held on to see out a 2-1 victory over Real Salt Lake and record their first victory since late September.

In an action-packed first half at PayPal Park, Ousseni Bouda and Benjamin Kikanovic netted in a 15-minute spell to put the Quakes in a commanding lead, and after Juan Sanabria halved the deficit with a 23rd-minute strike, the home side did well to repel Real Salt Lake and leave with all three points.

Prior to that, San Jose saw their nine-game unbeaten league streak come to an end on October 25, when they were hammered 3-0 by FC Dallas at the Toyota Stadium, four days before playing out a 2-2 stalemate with Colorado Rapids on home turf.

After enduring a disappointing 2025 campaign that saw them finish 10th in the West and narrowly miss out on the playoffs, Bruce Arena’s men have enjoyed a significant turnaround this season, collecting 52 points from 33 games to sit third in the conference standings, three points behind second-placed Dallas.

With playoff qualification already assured, San Jose will be keen to finish the regular season on a high, but a run of just one win in eight matches since August suggests they still have work to do before the campaign concludes.

San Jose Earthquakes Major League Soccer form:

Experienced midfielder Wil Trapp has missed each of Minnesota United’s last three matches due to the MLS concussion protocol, and the 33-year-old will play no part in Sunday’s finale.

American youngster Kayne Rizvanovich was left out of the team list against Los Angeles FC last time out, and the 19-year-old goalkeeper is also expected to sit out this weekend's matchup.

Kelvin Yeboah has been a standout performer for Minnesota this season, and the Italian striker, who has racked up 18 goals and four assists in 29 league starts, will be one to keep an eye on.

San Jose Earthquakes will be without several players down the spine of the team, including Darius Johnson and Jonathan Gonzalez, who have been ruled out through injuries.

Nigerian forward Nonso Adimabua is currently recuperating from a muscle problem while DeJuan Jones continues his lengthy spell on the sidelines through an Achilles tendon injury.
